analysis.title: Prime Insights & Analytics Chart Pack - Asia (November 2026)
key_insights: Asia-focused Fundamental L/S managers are down 1.6% MTD through Nov 19 versus MXAP -5.6%. The drawdown came from beta and alpha on Info Tech tilts, Japan and Volatility factors. YTD is 12.4% (weighted average).
Asia YTD dispersion is high: the simple average is 6.3% and the median is 0.2%, against the 12.4% weighted average.
China-focused Fundamental L/S managers are down 1.4% MTD with YTD at 15.1%. MTD and YTD returns are driven by AI-space investments.
Japan-focused managers are down 2.0% MTD versus MXJP down 4%, with YTD at 7.6%. Beta drove the MTD drawdown more than alpha, and median YTD performance is 2%.
Global Fundamental L/S managers are down 0.7% MTD and up 8.4% YTD. Global Systematic managers are up 1.6% MTD and 17.9% YTD.
The Global Prime book had large net selling MTD, driven by long sales, with North America and Asia leading.
Asian Info Tech/AI saw heavy net selling, with long sales exceeding short sales 2.4 to 1. Flows were risk-off, with Emerging Markets dominating the selling and de-grossing over Developed Markets.
Taiwan and Korea led net selling, with hedge funds unwinding longs and adding new shorts. Net allocation to Taiwan is back to February levels and Korea to early January levels.

Net allocation to Asia in the Global Prime book fell 260 bps MTD to 24.3%, an 8.2% overweight versus MSCI World. That compares with a ~20% overweight in mid-June, and the level is back to late January.
Gross allocation to Asia fell 66 bps to 23.4%, a 7.2% overweight versus MSCI World.
9 of 11 sectors were net sold in Asia MTD. Info Tech led, followed by Industrials and Consumer Discretionary. Utilities and Consumer Staples saw marginal buying.

Info Tech remains 10.3% overweight versus MXAP, down from a ~22% peak in June and from 11% at the start of the year. This is a YTD low for the overweight. Semis and Electronic Equipment led the outflows.
Industrials was the second most sold Asia sector, with China dominating the long selling, partly offset by net buying in Taiwan, Australia and Korea. Its overweight versus MXAP rose to 4%.

Consumer Discretionary was the third most sold Asia sector, led by China, and is 1% underweight versus MXAP. Utilities was the most net bought sector, led by Japan and Australia, and sits 0.2% underweight versus MXAP.
Global Book gross leverage fell 1.7 pts MoM to 313% (95th percentile over 5 years). Net fell 4.6 pts to 68%, near 3-year lows (20th percentile over 5 years).
Fundamental L/S gross leverage fell 6.2 pts to 205.7% (77th percentile over 5 years). Net fell 9.0 pts to 40.6%, a 5-year low.
Asia Fundamental L/S net leverage fell 47.4 points MoM to 10%, the lowest in the records (over a decade). Gross fell 2.9% to 189.3% (10th percentile over 1 year, 55th over 5 years).
Fundamental L/S Momentum exposure fell sharply MTD for both Global and Asia managers. Asia managers now have negative Momentum exposure, last seen in 2022.

China net allocation is 6.7% (6th percentile over 5 years) and gross is 6.6% (69th percentile). Japan net allocation fell to 7.8% (87th percentile over 5 years) and gross to 7.5% (90th percentile over 5 years).

Korea net allocation fell to 2.3% (82nd percentile over 5 years) and gross to 2.1%. Taiwan net allocation fell to 4.4% (85th percentile over 5 years) and gross to 3.8%. Long and short sales contributed in both markets.

sector_views.rationale: Still the most overweight sector in Asia at 10.3% versus MXAP despite heavy net selling and de-grossing. The overweight is at its YTD low.
Overweight versus MXAP rose to 4% even though the sector was the second most net sold MTD.
One of the overweight sectors in Asia versus MXAP and net sold MTD.
The most underweight Asia sector versus MXAP, followed by Comm Services and Consumer Discretionary.
Most net bought Asia sector MTD, led by long buys in Japan and Australia, and near market weight at 0.2% underweight.

risk_factors: The AI sell-off in Asian equities continues, with Info Tech/AI the main source of net selling and de-grossing.
Dispersion among Asia managers is elevated, with a median YTD return of 0.2% against a weighted average of 12.4%.
Taiwan and Korea saw both long unwinds and new shorts from hedge funds.
vol_and_positioning: Global Book gross leverage is 313% (95th percentile over 5 years) and net is 68% (20th percentile over 5 years, near 3-year lows).
Fundamental L/S net leverage is 40.6%, a 5-year low, and gross is 205.7% (77th percentile over 5 years).
Asia Fundamental L/S net leverage is 10%, the lowest in over a decade of records, with gross at 189.3%.
Asia Fundamental L/S Momentum exposure is negative, last seen in 2022. Global Fundamental L/S Momentum exposure also fell sharply MTD.
Asia Info Tech long sales exceeded short sales 2.4 to 1 MTD.
